study type: Observational study (retrospective cohort using claims data)
cohort: The study included 436,991 deliveries (145,061 cesarean section; 291,930 vaginal) identified from a large U.S. commercial health care claims database in 2019 and 2020.
finding: Cesarean section deliveries were associated with a higher prevalence of most maternal and infant adverse outcomes, particularly respiratory conditions in infants, compared to vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with higher adjusted odds of severe maternal morbidity at 42 and 360 days, and higher adjusted odds of most adverse infant outcomes, especially respiratory morbidity, compared to vaginal delivery.
